- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.6) and forecast is below recent highs, adjust upward to reflect bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.3) and forecast is above recent lows, adjust downward to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; reduce forecasted overshoot by 5–15% in the immediate aftermath.  
- If sentiment is neutral or volatile (0.3–0.6), model should not overreact to short-term noise; use 3–5 day moving average smoothing.  
- Mean reversion bias is common in early forecast windows; if forecast is significantly above 10-day moving average, reduce by 10–20% for next period.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in 3 consecutive days, assume momentum bias and adjust next forecast upward by 5–10%.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, forecast should lag slightly behind true price to avoid over-leveraging bullish expectations.
